No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result TAJBank Sees BAFI Award As Renewed Call To Deepen Financial Inclusion by Olushola Bello 10 seconds ago in Business Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram TAJBank Limited has described its fifth consecutive Non-Interest Bank of the Year Award as more than recognition of past performance, saying it renews the bank’s commitment to deepen financial inclusion and expand access to ethical, customer-focused banking.
The bank received the award at BusinessDay Media Limited’s 2026 Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards, where it was again named Non-Interest Bank of the Year.
The founder and managing director of TAJBank, Hamid Joda, said the recognition strengthened TAJBank’s responsibility to serve individuals, businesses and underserved communities through transparent and accessible financial services.
“We see this award not merely as a celebration of our achievements, but as a renewed call to deepen financial inclusion, strengthen our commitment to ethical banking and develop innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers,” Joda said in a statement by the bank’s head of Marketing Communications, Isiaka Wakili.
“We are deeply honoured to receive the Non-Interest Bank of the Year Award at the 2026 BAFI Awards.”
He said the recognition belonged to the bank’s Board of Directors, management, dedicated staff and, most importantly, its valued customers, whose confidence continued to inspire the institution.
In his remarks, the co-founder/executive director of TAJBank, Sheriff Idi, said the award reflected the bank’s progress in building a distinctive identity in Nigeria’s financial services industry.
He noted that TAJBank had continued to strengthen its market position through customer-focused solutions, operational innovation and a business model designed to meet the diverse financial needs of its growing clientele.
He said the award would spur the bank to consolidate its gains, explore new growth opportunities and deliver greater value to customers while reinforcing its position in the nation’s non-interest banking sector.
The publisher/CEO of BusinessDay Media Ltd, Frank Aigbogun, noted that “to be recognised as Non-Interest Bank of the Year is to be acknowledged as an institution demonstrating that banking can simultaneously deliver profitability, trust and responsible financial stewardship.”
Aigbogun said that, in a financial landscape increasingly shaped by questions of sustainability, ethics and long-term trust, TAJBank had distinguished itself as one of Nigeria’s most dynamic and credible non-interest financial institutions.
